COMMITTING: git push is 403 'denied to Onyx-Node' for the fixer too, not only for subagents - the App has no write access to kavopdf/app over HTTPS git. It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. The next run should commit that way, then 'git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main' so HEAD matches origin, then chain.py. chain.py's sync check is strict SHA equality and also refuses a dirty tree, and it rewrites CHAIN.json - so commit CHAIN.json again after each chain.py run.

history.plan: READ FINDINGS/content-present-partly-displaced-rules-are-flow-neutral-065000-f1x.md BEFORE TOUCHING THE RULE CLASS. Two handoff claims are now measured FALSE: (1) the flush-by-top precondition is a regression, not a precondition - with the border path OFF it takes bank-statement 0.10 -> 17.07 and gst-invoice 0.38 -> 15.13, because every shape moved into the flow charges ~9.6 pt; (2) the residual on 18_displacement was never the gap or the flowY bookkeeping - a carrier paragraph costs 9.6 pt in LibreOffice whatever it contains (measured four ways), which is the whole of 0.00 -> 77.01. A flow-neutral construct exists and is in FINDINGS/rules-top-border-FLOW-NEUTRAL-065000-f1x.patch: a pre-pass hands each rule to the paragraph that follows it as a w:top border, the gap becomes w:before and the rule-to-text distance becomes w:space, nothing is reordered and no paragraph is added. It measures EXACTLY baseline on all 8 documents tried (18_centred 0.00, 411 0.00, 62 0.00, bank-statement 0.10, gst-invoice 0.38, mobile-bill 1.55, 315 1.91, 64 3.46) - and places pBdr=0, because its own safety guards decline every rule it could reach. Where a border IS placed, 18_centred goes 0.00 -> 0.53. THAT is the wall and it is not an engine bug: regress.py scores share@5 on a LibreOffice render, LibreOffice draws the floating drawing exactly, and a border can never be pixel-identical - so a fix Google needs is always a small LibreOffice regression, and the brief forbids landing one. DO NOT start another rule-class attempt until a human answers: gate this class in Google (32_stroke_lines / 05_chars_extra on the Google result), declare the class out of scope, or authorise a stated tolerance. Spend the next slot on a class the gate can see.

Measure the reach of every construct before building the next one: 47_margins has 26 documents and the two constructs on the table reach 3 and 5 of them, so the class was being attacked from the wrong end. Traced all 26, corrected SETTLED's run-size lead, added verify_google --detail so a FAIL names its page and its distance.
